content.title: When Technology Leads Your Child Astray—Learn How to Protect Them!
content.subtitle: A remarkable solution from the lives of the Salaf.
content.body:
Returning home after an exhausting day, you are met with a painful sight: your child refuses to put down their phone. Oblivious to your presence, their gaze remains trapped in the glow of the screen. A sharp ache grips your chest—a bitter mix of silent fatigue and lingering fear.

We live in unforgiving times. Temptations and fitnah loom from every corner. Shielding our children from these pervasive digital currents feels almost impossible. Screens, social media algorithms, and endless digital traps are quietly consuming their inner world. For parents, this helplessness is deeply agonizing.

An Outburst of Anger or a Poisonous Arrow?

But what do we do in such moments?

We lose patience. Our tempers rise, and shouting, harsh words, and even verbal abuse begin. In anger, words like “Go to Hell!” or “You will never amount to anything!” may slip from our tongues.

But have we ever considered that when our child is already drifting in the current of fitnah, our harsh words may push them even deeper into darkness? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ warned: “Do not supplicate against yourselves, and do not supplicate against your children, lest it coincide with a time when Allah is asked and He grants what is asked.” — (Sahih Muslim: 3009)

The Tears and Self-Reflection of the Salaf

Children also grew up in the homes of our righteous predecessors. They too faced disobedience and deviation among their children. But instead of giving in to anger, they turned to Allah.

When the Tabi‘i Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad (RA) saw his son ‘Ali becoming increasingly arrogant and disobedient, he did not scold or curse him. Instead, he stood on his prayer mat at night, raised his hands, and wept: “O Allah! I have exhausted myself trying to teach this child good manners, and I can no longer do it. O my Lord, You teach him manners and the Deen on my behalf.” — (Siyar A‘lam al-Nubala: 8/443)

Allah did not turn away that heartfelt plea. His son ‘Ali later became one of the most righteous and God-fearing people of his time.

The Tabi‘i Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir (RA) would also spend nights in Tahajjud, hoping that through his heartfelt supplications, Allah would keep his child firm upon guidance. (Al-Hilyah: 3/153)

Two Paths to the Solution: Companionship by Day, Sujood by Night

We often think that enrolling our children in a good school or madrasa, hiring a tutor, and providing everything they need means our responsibility is complete. No. Our responsibility has only begun. To protect your child from the fire of fitnah, hold firmly to these two things:

  • Be Their Friend During the Day: Break down the walls of fear. Sit beside your child and listen. Build a safe space at home where they can freely share what is in their heart before turning to harmful influences outside. Pull them close, kiss their forehead, and say: “I love you so much. Tell me everything in your heart. Who could be a better friend to you than me?”

  • Surrender Through Tears at Night: When the world falls asleep, place your face in sujood during Tahajjud. Raise your hands and say: “O Allah! I cannot protect my child from the fitnah of this world. This child is Your trust. Protect my amanah with Your divine power.”

Remember, a heart that cannot be softened by discipline or resentment can become soft as wax through the mercy of the Lord of the Throne.
